newsitem.title: FRANCE: France fears Cyprus missiles may fuel arms race.
newsitem.headline: France fears Cyprus missiles may fuel arms race.

text.p: France expressed fears on Friday that Cyprus's plan to deploy anti-aircraft missiles to neutralise Turkish air superiority could spur a regional arms race and called on Ankara to show restraint.

French Foreign Ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt said that Paris had expressed its concerns to Nicosia about its plan to buy Russian missiles and was urging a revival of talks to end the division of the island since 1974.

"We consider that deployment of S-300 missiles in the context of over-armament poses a major risk of escalation both on the island and in the region," he told reporters, adding that France recognised Nicosia's right to self-defence.

"We are counting on the maturity and sense of restraint by the authorities in Ankara to abstain from any gesture that might increase tension in the region and affect Turkey's relations with its main partners, including the Europeans," he said.

Turkey has accused the Cypriot government of trying to change the balance of forces on the island by a deal announced over the weekend to buy Russian anti-aircraft missiles that could neutralise Turkish air superiority.
There are 30,000 Turkish troops in the northern third of Cyprus while the internationally-recognised Cyprus government controls the Greek Cypriot south.
The island has been divided since 1974, when Turkish troops invaded in response to a coup engineered by the military junta then ruling Greece.
